rawOutput.title: Personal Finance Fundamentals
rawOutput.topic: Budgeting, credit, debt, and index-fund investing
rawOutput.rationale: This four-session sequence treats personal finance as conceptual learning plus practical problem solving. It begins with a financial baseline, teaches unfamiliar credit and interest concepts, then connects debt repayment with basic index-fund investing. The final session checks retrieval and application through an integrated financial scenario. Sessions use manageable content slices, practical examples, and support based on each attempt.

sessions.title: Build a Practical Budgeting Baseline
sessions.objective: Create a simple monthly cash-flow plan and identify a realistic financial buffer.
sessions.amountLabel: One monthly budget and one emergency-buffer decision
contentTargets: Income, fixed expenses, variable expenses, and savings
A basic emergency fund and handling irregular expenses
completionEvidence: Classify sample transactions as income, fixed expenses, variable expenses, or savings
Construct a balanced monthly budget from a sample income and expense list
Explain one adjustment that would create room for an emergency buffer

sessions.title: Understand Credit and Interest
sessions.objective: Explain how borrowing costs and common credit behaviors affect a balance and credit record.
sessions.amountLabel: Three credit concepts applied to one card example
contentTargets: Simple and compound interest as borrowing costs
Credit-card statements, minimum payments, and grace periods
Payment history and credit utilization as major credit factors
completionEvidence: Explain why paying only the minimum can keep debt active for longer
Apply APR information to compare two simplified borrowing offers
Demonstrate how an on-time payment and a lower card balance can affect credit factors

sessions.title: Connect Debt Repayment and Index-Fund Investing
sessions.objective: Compare debt priorities with long-term investing and explain the basic role of diversified index funds.
sessions.amountLabel: One debt-priority decision and one index-fund explanation
contentTargets: Debt prioritization using interest rates, minimum payments, and cash-flow stability
Index funds, diversification, fees, risk, and long-term returns
completionEvidence: Classify sample debts by repayment urgency using interest rate and consequence of missed payment
Explain how an index fund differs from choosing one company’s stock
Compare paying high-interest debt with investing when returns are uncertain

sessions.title: Apply the Fundamentals to One Financial Plan
sessions.objective: Retrieve and combine budgeting, credit, debt, and investing principles in a realistic scenario.
sessions.amountLabel: One integrated case covering all four fundamentals
contentTargets: An integrated monthly plan balancing expenses, emergency savings, debt, and investing
Credit and investment tradeoffs under changing financial conditions
completionEvidence: Construct a monthly allocation for a sample household without prompts
Explain the order chosen for bills, emergency savings, debt payments, and investing
Apply one changed circumstance to revise the plan and justify the revision
